question: What Windows installer TLS recovery policy should OpenClaw ship when `install.ps1` reaches an npm leaf-certificate verification failure?
rationale: The bug blocks first-time Windows setup, but the obvious retry path changes npm package-install TLS verification, so automation should not choose the trust boundary.

options.title: Security-reviewed CA remediation
options.body: Detect the TLS failure and guide or apply explicit `cafile` or `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` remediation without automatically bypassing certificate verification.

options.title: Operator-approved insecure retry
options.body: Allow a clearly warned interactive-only `--strict-ssl=false` retry while failing non-interactive installs with remediation instructions.

options.title: Documentation-only workaround
options.body: Keep the installer fail-closed and document npm `cafile`, Windows Hub, or WSL2 alternatives for affected environments.

recommendation.title: Security-reviewed CA remediation
recommendation.body: Detect the TLS failure and guide or apply explicit `cafile` or `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` remediation without automatically bypassing certificate verification.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history on Windows installer failure handling and hardening.
